Ben/Laura —

Forwarding Samir's traffic profile and procurement constraints. Highlights for pricing policy:
- Monthly true-ups required by the buyer (procurement@aetherlabs.com)
- Lock pricing for 6 months post-signature if possible
- Need a surge allowance that covers campaign-week peaks (~420M tokens/day) without blowing their monthly invoice unexpectedly

Ben — can you sketch a stepped commit schedule that results in predictable monthly invoices and accommodates procurement's monthly true-up ask? I'm thinking a baseline commit that maps to 70% of expected month-1 avg, a month-2 step to 85%, and a month-4 step to 100%. Also propose how much capped surge credit to include and whether we need a small onboarding credit for the pilot.

Laura — anything in our standard wording that blocks monthly true-ups or the 6-month price protection?

Thanks,
Jasmine

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.dev>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.dev>, Samir Shah <samir@aetherlabs.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.dev>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.dev>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial worksheet: monthly ramp + seasonal buffer

Team / Samir —

Sketching a practical structure that meets procurement's monthly true-up ask and keeps invoices predictable:

1) Commit tiers (monthly):
   - Month 0 (pilot, billable at discounted pilot rate): 3.5B tokens total for the 2-week pilot month (prepaid credit).
   - Month 1 baseline commit: 6.5B tokens (covers ~70% of avg day x 30).
   - Month 2 step-up: 8.0B tokens.
   - Month 3: hold at 8.0B tokens (allows smoothing).
   - Month 4 step-up: 9.2B tokens (matches expected steady-state).

2) Surge allowance: 15% capped on top of monthly commit as a non-invoiced buffer; any usage beyond the cap triggers the monthly true-up at the committed per-token rate (no surprise list-rate billing).

3) True-ups and invoicing: monthly reconciliation — if actual usage > commit + surge cap, charge increment at the committed per-token price. If actual usage < commit, no refund but can apply small credit toward future months (one-time true-up credit).

4) Price protection: 6 months lock on per-token price starting at signing. We can offer a one-time onboarding credit of $12,000 to offset pilot tuning costs.

I'll put numbers into the attached workbook and propose a signed SOW addendum that captures monthly true-ups and surge caps.

Vivek — tagging you for approval on the onboarding credit and the 15% surge policy for a strategic customer.

Ben

Thanks Ben — I approve the structure in principle. A few quick operational constraints to capture in the SOW:

- Limit the onboarding credit to costs clearly associated with the pilot (tied to the two-week window).
- Include a one-time capacity guarantee clause for the first 60 days (best-effort dedicated pool + prioritized routing) — subject to availability and at Redwood's discretion with a rollback clause if we observe sustained >120% of commit.
- For the surge cap, let's add a notification threshold at 90% usage so Aether can be warned before we hit the cap.

Samir — if that looks good to you I can ask legal to draft the SOW addendum with monthly true-ups, price protection for 6 months, surge cap at 15% with a 90% notify, and the onboarding credit language.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

This is great and addresses our main concerns. Two small asks before we proceed to legal:
1) Can the onboarding credit be applied as an invoice credit (to keep our month-to-month cashflow consistent)?
2) Slight tweak to surge cap: would you consider a 20% cap for the first month only (given the campaign peaks) and then revert to 15% for months 2–3?

If you can accept those two items, procurement is ready to take the SOW to signature and we can route invoices monthly as requested.

Samir
